description:
Think about the last time you said yes to a favor you absolutely dreaded.

That's the question at the center of The Art of Saying NO by Damon Zahariades: why do we agree to requests that drain our time and energy, and how do we decline without feeling like we've failed the people we care about?

This is a summary and discussion of the book's argument. We cover the idea that every yes is a withdrawal from a limited account of time and energy, why guilt pushes so many of us to agree, how a clear, early no can be more respectful than a vague maybe, and what the book admits is hard about holding a boundary.
